title: ChatGPT points to a blood pressure medication behind an 18-month cough that doctors had not explained; a doctor confirms it and changes the prescription, and X user Shreya reports her mother healing
summary: ChatGPT flagged a BP drug side effect behind an 18-month cough; a doctor confirmed it and changed the drug; daughter reports mother healing.
account: On 23 July 2025 an X user posting as Shreya.tsx (@Life_of_coder, profile location 'india') wrote that her mother had had a nonstop cough for 1.5 years despite top doctors, big hospitals in and outside their city, homeopathy, ayurveda and allopathy; internal bleeding had begun, and doctors had warned the condition could be fatal within six months. She described everything to OpenAI's ChatGPT, which listed possible causes including blood pressure medication and asked whether the prescription contained a specific ingredient; it did. A doctor, told of this, confirmed it at once and changed the medication, and her mother was 'finally healing'. Four Indian outlets reported the post on 24 July 2025; it has since been deleted.
purpose: ChatGPT is OpenAI's general-purpose conversational assistant, not a diagnostic or drug-safety tool; surfacing a medication side effect as the likely cause of a chronic cough was outside what it was built for, so the benefit is marked unexpected.
segment: Consumer use by a patient's adult daughter
taxonomy_note: Knowledge Discovery is the nearest fit for a diagnostic lead surfaced to a family member; the taxonomy has no patient-health category. Benefit created or restored rather than specific harm prevented: the post says doctors had warned the illness 'could be fatal', so a harm may have been averted, but the only account is the daughter's own since-deleted post as relayed by Indian outlets; no clinician, hospital, prescription or medical record was published, and neither the drug nor the 'ingredient' is named. Dated 23 July 2025, the day of the post (X API capture at 12:26:51 UTC); the Monitor's 24 July is the first day of news coverage, and the dates of the consultation and the medication change are not given. The poster's profile gives 'india' as location and the Monitor codes the country as India; the city is unnamed, so location is left null. The account @Life_of_coder was created on 27 January 2025 and had 4,237 followers when the post was captured; on 20 October 2026 X's syndication endpoint returned 'This Post was deleted by the Post author'.

ratings.reason: One identifiable patient, the poster's mother, had an 18-month cough with internal bleeding that doctors had warned could become fatal; after the medication change her daughter reported her 'finally healing'. Material for one person; rated below life-changing because the recovery was in progress and nothing beyond the daughter's post documents the diagnosis or the outcome.

ai_role.statement: ChatGPT generated the hypothesis: among several possible causes it listed blood pressure medication, and when told the mother was on such medication it asked whether the prescription contained a specific ingredient, which it did. The confirmation and the prescription change were made by a doctor ('He confirmed it instantly and changed the meds'). A commenter quoted by NDTV, Mint, Mashable India and the Financial Express says cough is a known side effect of BP medicine that doctors 'should've checked', which frames the contribution as surfacing a documented side effect rather than a novel diagnosis. No clinician comments on the chatbot's role, and the whole sequence rests on the daughter's account.

produced_by: A family member with an 18-month symptom history (nonstop cough, then internal bleeding) who described it all to ChatGPT after top doctors, big hospitals, homeopathy, ayurveda and allopathy had not helped
ChatGPT listed several possible causes, including blood pressure medication, and, told the mother was on BP medication, asked whether it contained a specific ingredient, which it did
A doctor who, told of the suggestion, confirmed it at once and changed the prescription
must_hold: The chatbot's suggestion is taken to a prescribing doctor who confirms it before any medication is changed; the post credits the doctor with both the confirmation and the change
The cough must actually be the drug's side effect; the post names neither the drug nor the 'ingredient', so the mechanism cannot be checked against the drug's label
The account rests on one since-deleted post by the patient's daughter, relayed by independent outlets; no clinician, hospital or record corroborates it

headline: ChatGPT traces an 18-month cough to a BP drug; doctor confirms

revisions.change: Record drafted from the OECD Monitor entry and the cited sources.

claim_basis: Seven independent news reports, one other independent source and the beneficiary's other are on file. There is no independent study or report and no finding by a regulator or court.
